posing_source.statement: R(1,k)=x_k; R(n,k)=R(n-1,k+1)-sum_(j=1..n-1) binom(n-2,j-1)R(j,k)R(n-j,1), n>=2, k>=1; R(n,1)=L_n where log(1+sum_(i>=1)x_i t^i/i!)=sum_(n>=1)L_n t^n/n!.

written_proofs.statement: R(n,k)=(n-1)![t^(n-1)]F^(k)/F for every n,k>=1 over any commutative rational algebra.
written_proofs.mechanism: The quotients Q_k=F^(k)/F satisfy Q_k'=Q_(k+1)-Q_k Q_1; coefficient extraction and simultaneous induction give the array.

written_proofs.statement: R(n,k)=kappa(Z^k,Z,...,Z), with n-1 copies of Z and the unital formal functional Phi(Z^i)=x_i. The two-factor product-cumulant identity gives the exact binomial recurrence by counting subsets of n-2 labels.
written_proofs.attribution: Leonov–Shiryaev (1959); Beuman–Turner–Vitelli (2012), Appendix A, (A10)–(A15); Burchardt (2018), Section 1.2 and Theorem 1.9.

written_proofs.statement: Partition coefficient formula; term counts, row sums, Stirling specialization, moment/Appell identities, reciprocal formula, six cycle/Bell/Lah substitutions, Faber scaling, matrix conjugation, signed A130850 specialization.
L_n=-(n-1)!sum_j rho_j^(-n) for n>=2 for the canonical product with zero Gaussian factor; a Gaussian factor changes L_2 by -2a.
F=(1-t)e^t gives P_3(z)=(z+1)^2(z-2). More generally F=e^(beta t)p(t) with deg(p)=d gives multiplicity n-d at -beta for n>d.
written_proofs.attribution: Exponential-polynomial exception: Craven and Csordas (1994), Proposition 4.1(2).

classical_sources.authors: V. P. Leonov and A. N. Shiryaev
classical_sources.coverage: Product-cumulant theorem; algebraic formulation in Burchardt, Theorem 1.9.
